name: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd

items.statement: FY26 pre-sales target Rs 1,100-1,300 crore, revenue growth 75-85%, PAT growth 30-35%
items.quote: For FY '26, we are targeting pre-sales of about Rs. 1,100 crores to Rs. 1,300 crores. Revenue growth of about 75% to 85%, and PAT growth of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Annual pre-sales growth 3x-5x over next three years
items.quote: So, we are expecting annual growth 3x to 5x for next three years. And that will be overall growth of 3x to 5x.

items.statement: Portfolio of ~3 million sq ft carpet area, ~2.3 million sq ft saleable, GDV Rs 12,000-13,000 crore by FY30
items.quote: Together, this translates into a portfolio of about 3 million square feet of carpet area, of which approximately 2.3 million square feet will be saleable. This is expected to deliver a gross development value in the range of Rs. 12,000 crores to Rs. 13,000 crores by FY '30.

items.statement: Three launches by September 2025: Arcadian Juhu, Amalfi Versova, Varun Bandra; total saleable 2.2 lakh sq ft, GDV Rs 1,400-1,500 crore
items.quote: The total saleable carpet area of these three projects, the Arcadian that is in Juhu, Amalfi in Versova, and Varun in Bandra-Carter Road is 2.2 lakh square feet with the estimated GD V of Rs. 1,400 crores to Rs. 1,500 crores

items.statement: Six launches planned in FY26 with GDV ~Rs 4,500 crore, targeted pre-sales Rs 750-850 crore from these
items.quote: So, we are launching these three projects and other three projects, total six projects we are launching . And the current year pre -sale from this is around Rs. 750 crores to Rs. 850 crores and the GDV is approximately Rs 3,000 crores (Mentioned Rs 2,000 crores mistakenly on the call) for the year.

items.statement: Four new projects added in FY26 with GDV Rs 3,700-4,000 crore; seven to eight projects locked for FY27-28
items.quote: So, all four projects we have estimated GDV is approximately Rs. 3,700 crores to Rs. 4,000 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 EBITDA margin 48%; high margins driven by zero debt, zero marketing spend, fast execution, 20% premium pricing
items.quote: EBITDA was Rs. 29.5 crores, EBITDA margin stood at 48%

items.statement: Commercial project margins expected in line with residential segment
items.quote: And we are expecting the margins to be in line with the residential segment.

items.statement: Average revenue per sq ft Rs 40,000-60,000 last year; expected to rise with coastal and new micro-market projects
items.quote: last year we had an average of revenue per square feet was between Rs. 40,000 to Rs. 60,000 a square feet, which is quite decent, quite high. But looking forward, the way we have mounted our new projects, which are more on coastline, we are expecting that this per square feet revenue will go up.

items.statement: Demand for ultra-luxury products constantly rising; no slowdown concerns in niche segment
items.quote: The demand is, I would say, for our kind of product, demand is constantly going up because everyone wants to move from lower strata of the pyramid to above strata of pyramid.

items.statement: Rs 165 crore invested in three September-launch projects till June 2025
items.quote: So, Yes, total investment for all these three projects is already we have incurred Rs. 165 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 collections Rs 70 crore vs pre-sales Rs 61.3 crore; inventory ~Rs 200 crore in completed projects
items.quote: Collection for this quarter was Rs. 70 crores

items.statement: Net debt-free with net cash Rs 905 crore as of August 2025; IPO net proceeds Rs 732 crore deployed Rs 88.7 crore till 22 Aug
items.quote: As of August 2025, we are net debt-free with net cash balance of Rs 905 crores.

items.statement: IPO raised Rs 792 crore fresh issue; net proceeds Rs 732 crore post expenses
items.quote: During the IPO , we raised Rs. 792 crores through fres h issue and net proceeds post -issue expenses was Rs. 732 crores.

items.statement: Project cycle less than 4 years; typically 3-4 years to complete
items.quote: our project cycle is less than four years , so normally three and four years we will be able to seal the project.

items.statement: 87% units sold before OC in Ananya, 45% Signature, 42% Ayana, 56% Arc One; ~25% sales from referrals, zero marketing spend
items.quote: 87% of units in Ananya were sold before OC, 45% at Signature, 42% at Ananya and 56% at Arc One.

items.statement: First-mover advantage in ultra-luxury redevelopment; 7 completed projects; no direct competition in ultra-luxury category
items.quote: we have completed about seven redevelopment projects. That's one. Second is, we have handed over all those projects in ultra -luxury category. So, in that category, I do not remember any other developer is there.

items.statement: DCPR 2034 and subsequent policy changes very friendly for redevelopment; Supreme Court clearance removes NGT approval backlog
items.quote: I think now it has been cleared by Supreme Court. So, I feel that everyone, not only us, but all the developers who had that backlog, that will be cleared very soon.

items.statement: Zero RERA cases or complaints in company history
items.quote: Importantly, we have never had a single RERA case or even RERA complaints against us on any of our projects in its history.

items.statement: Societies now approach Lotus directly for redevelopment partnerships due to brand reputation
items.quote: So, generally, now since we have made our brand in redevelopment, ultra-luxury developer, we get invitation. And all the societies, I mean, who wants to redevelop, they think about Lotus as one of the partners.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue recognition depends on project milestones; Q1 modest due to no launches
items.quote: Quarterly revenue recognized depends on project milestones. And as we all know, this is not like any FMCG or IT.

items.statement: Feed sales for FY26 estimated at 5,60,000 metric tons
items.quote: We are expecting about 5,60,000 metric tons of feed for this year.

items.statement: Shrimp exports for FY26 estimated at 17,000 metric tons
items.quote: It is estimated that the exports during FY26 would be around 17,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Pet food sales target for FY26 set at INR 10 crore
items.quote: We have a target of INR 10 crore for this year.

items.statement: Pet care manufacturing plant construction to start by end of FY26
items.quote: The company is planning to commence the construction by end of this year after obtaining necessary government approvals.

items.statement: U.S. 50% reciprocal tariff impact on shrimp exports, especially second season
items.quote: The forecast for the second half of this year is challenging due to factors like gradual increase of raw material prices and levy of reciprocal tariff by U.S. at the rate of 50%.

items.statement: Raw material prices expected to rise, impacting margins
items.quote: The prices of fish meals increased to INR 93 per kg in Q1 FY 26 from INR 91 per kg in Q4 FY 25 and decreased from INR 117 per kg in Q1 FY 25. In case of soybean meal, prices reduced to INR 39 per kg in Q1 FY26 from INR 40 in Q4 FY25 and INR 49 in Q1 FY25

items.statement: Heavy rains and diseases temporarily slowed aquaculture activity
items.quote: Initially, the culture started very well and it was progressing, but due to heavy rains, there were premature harvest and som e diseases here and there, have actually temporarily slowed down the aquaculture activity

items.statement: Feed prices cut by INR 4/kg in April FY26
items.quote: We have recently cut our prices by INR 4.

items.statement: U.S. tariff costs being passed on to customers
items.quote: So, we're definitely passing it on to the customer.

items.statement: Shift to value-added shrimp products for better margins
items.quote: The focus is on demand for value-added products, which is gradually increasing and processes see better margins in value-added products.

items.statement: U.S. holiday season shipments partially completed, some ongoing
items.quote: A good portion of it is completed, at least for Avanti. We did ship out a considerable amount of product in the first quarter. That's why you see a huge jump in revenue, but there are always parts of it which need to be shipped out.

items.statement: Diversification into Japan, Europe, Canada, and Middle East markets underway
items.quote: Keeping this factor in view, the endeavo ur of the company is to expand its global market to other destinations like Japan, Korea, European Union and Middle-East

items.statement: Fish feed manufacturing CapEx planned post-trial success
items.quote: If we find a suitable feed appropriate for Indian fish culture then we'll be able to set up the manufacturing facility.

items.statement: Merger of Dr. Agarwal's Eye Hospital (AEHL) into Dr. Agarwal's Health Care (AHCL) announced with share swap ratio of 23 AHCL shares for every 2 AEHL shares
items.quote: The scheme provides for merging of AEHL with AHCL, creating a single listed entity, combining business operations of both the entities.

items.statement: Independent valuers PWC and Bansi Mehta recommended share swap ratio; fairness opinions from Kotak Mahindra Capital and Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors
items.quote: PWC Business Consulting Services, LLP and Bansi S. Mehta Valuers, LLP, the Independent Valuers acted as the joint valuation advisors and have recommended a share s wap ratio of 23 equity shares of AHCL for every 2 shares of Agarwal Eye Hospital Limited

items.statement: Swap ratio implies 15% premium for AEHL shareholders over 10-day VWAP of INR 4,554 per share
items.quote: The swap ratio implies a 15% premium for AEHL over AEHL's 10-day VWAP of INR 4,554 per share.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of 1,32,827 AEHL shares to AHCL at Rs. 5,270 per share totalling Rs. 70 crores for Cathedral Road flagship facility capex
items.quote: AHCL will require 1,32,827 equity shares of AEHL at a price of Rs. 5,270 per share, amounting to a total investment of approximately Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Post-merger shareholding: AEHL public shareholders 4.6%, AHCL public 64.5% (down from 67.6%), promoters 30.9%; combined share capital ~Rs. 33.13 crores
items.quote: In terms of the post -merger shareholding of the combined entity, AEHL public shareholders will hold 4.6% stake in the combined entity. AH CL public shareholding will get diluted from 67.6% to 64.5%. Promoter and promoter group will hold close to 30.9% stake in the combined entity

items.statement: Merger expected to complete in 12-14 months subject to stock exchange/SEBI no-objection, NCLT approval, and majority of minority shareholder approval at both companies
items.quote: The implementation of the transaction is expected to take around 12-14 months, subject to requisite approvals.

items.statement: Special resolution required at both companies plus majority of minority approval per SEBI requirements
items.quote: So, for this merger, we have to pass a special resolution at both the company level, AHCL as well as A EHL from a company perspective . Also from SEBI perspective, we need to get the majority of minority approval as well

items.statement: Cost synergies expected from elimination of duplicate auditors, GST cross-charge tax leakage reduction, resource optimization, and lower filing costs
items.quote: Currently since we have two companies, in terms of the auditors, we have to have two separate auditors for both the companies. That is one major cost. Apart from that, in terms of cross-charge across both the entities, there will also be a significant reduction in tax leakage from GST perspective.

items.statement: Preferential allotment chosen over inter-company loan to avoid stress on AHCL balance sheet; AHCL has good cash reserves at holding company level
items.quote: We believe that instead of us putting any more stres s on the balance sheet at the AHCL level, we feel that this will be a better route for us to do a preferential

items.statement: Valuation used market value, comparable company, and DCF approaches with appropriate weights; reports approved by audit committees and boards of both companies
items.quote: The valuers have used several valuation methodologies, including market value, trading multiples, DCF, and also applied appropriate weights to these methods to arrive at the final value of each business.

items.statement: Minority shareholders of AEHL strongly oppose swap ratio as unfair; multiple investors request re-evaluation and separate valuation call
items.quote: I am just upset that the merger ratio is in favor of the holding company, right? Because if I were to just do a basic analysis of FY '25 Dr. Agarwal’s revenues, right, and I adjust the revenues of the holding company for the minority interest of the AEHL, the ratio should be more towards 15 -17 shares for each share held for the subsidiary

items.statement: Merger requires majority of minority approval at both AEHL and AHCL; if AEHL minority rejects, process subject to NCLT outcome
items.quote: On that, the process just require s the majority of minority approval at both AHCL as well as at the AEHL level

items.statement: Management commits to separate offline call with AEHL minority shareholders to explain valuation methodology and address concerns
items.quote: We are more than happy to meet with our AEHL minority shareholders offline and discuss this in detail. We can find a proper time and we can take you all through the details.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target above INR10,000 crores with INR3,000 crores from defense and INR7,000 crores from non-defense
items.quote: If you look at our annual guidance of INR10,000 crores, so we are still believ ing that we will definitely cross INR10,000 crores in this financial year. And out of that, INR3,000 crores should be some defense and nondefense should add to around INR7,000 crores

items.statement: International revenue expected at INR3,500-4,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: So in this year, if we have given a guidance of around INR10,000 crores, so we are expecting around INR4,000 crores from international market, INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Domestic explosives volume growth target of 15% for FY26
items.quote: So like we said that we are targeting around 15% volume growth in this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target around 27% for FY26
items.quote: So these factors, if you take into the account the achieving margin of around 27% is a reasonable expectation from our side.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR2,500 crores for FY26 with strategic expansion over coming years
items.quote: as we have shared in our annual call that we are going to invest INR2,500 crores in this financial year. And in the coming years also, we have a strong strategic program to expand our facilities

items.statement: Kazakhstan plant expected to start commercial production by October 2025
items.quote: Yes, we are trying to start our Kazakhstan plant in this financial year. Hopefully, by October, we should start the plant.

items.statement: Total defense order book of INR15,000 crores with INR8,000 crores from international markets
items.quote: like we have already shared that we have a total order book of around INR15,000 cr ores. And after leaving the Pinaka portion, the order book from international is around INR8,000 crores

items.statement: Early monsoon and milder heat waves reduced domestic explosives demand in Q1; recovery expected post-monsoon
items.quote: Mining industry had lower demand due to milder heat waves, early monsoon and geopolitical development tested the industry's resilience. However, we remain optimistic about the growth in mining and housing and infrastructure sector in the upcoming quarters and the domestic cycle revised post monsoon.

items.statement: Pinaka rocket commercialization expected from end of Q2 or start of Q3 FY26
items.quote: And as far as the products, which will give the momentum will be one of the key products is Pinaka series of rockets, should start from end of Q2 or start of the Q3.

items.statement: 155mm shell commercial production to start soon; Bhargavastra and Rudrastra in qualification phase
items.quote: So as far as this product is concerned, we have the facilities to make these products. We have already started working on that. And very soon, we will start the commercial production of this product.

items.statement: Nagastra 2 and 3 in development; entering higher altitude/longer endurance drone category with ZAL partnership
items.quote: So after a successful on the Nagastra 1, we have started making Nagastra 2 and Nagastra 3 also for some of the special applications. And as we are moving forward, definitely, it's a natural growth for us or it will be a natural growth for us to expand in the higher category of

items.statement: South Africa subsidiary driving above-normal international growth in Q1
items.quote: But as far as the momentum, which is above the normal momentum in the numbers is mainly on account of a very good business from South Africa because all subsidiaries are doing quite well, but South Africa is doing much better now compared to the couple of years back.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR50 crores as of June 2025, down from INR100+ crores at March 2025
items.quote: So as on 31st March 2025, we were INR100 crores plus net of cash position, and currently, we are at INR50 crores cash position positive.

items.statement: Hyperinflationary accounting applied to Turkey operations; INR18 crores P&L impact and INR9 crores reserve impact in Q1
items.quote: So we have hyperinflationary account in Turkey. So currently, the figures are around INR18 crores, which affected our P&L for this quarter, and INR9 crores in reserves.

items.statement: Q1 FY26: Revenue INR2,154 crores (+28% YoY), EBITDA INR564 crores (+19% YoY), PAT INR353 crores (+17% YoY)
items.quote: We achieved revenue of INR2154 crores versus INR1685 crores, increased by 28% year-on-year, highest quarterly EBITDA at INR564 crores versus INR474, increased by 19% year-on-year. PAT stands at INR353 crores versus INR301 crores, increased by 17% year-on-year.

items.statement: International revenue INR826 crores (+43% YoY), defense revenue INR418 crores (+115% YoY) in Q1
items.quote: International revenue was INR826 crores versus INR579 crores, registering highest quarterly revenue with a growth of 43%. Defense revenue was INR418 crores versus INR194 crores in the same quarter previous year, registering growth of 115%.

items.statement: Raw material cost 50.8% of sales vs 51.65% YoY; employee cost 8.53% vs 7.78%; other expenses 15.85% vs 13.90%
items.quote: Coming to the cost breakup, raw material consumption cost was 50.8% as a percentage of sales versus 51.65%. Employee costs was at 8.53% versus 7.78% as a percentage of sales. Other expense cost was approximately 15.85% versus 13.90% as a percentage of sales.

items.statement: Emergency drone procurement demand sustainability uncertain; difficult to comment on long-term demand
items.quote: Difficult for me to comment on this question.

items.statement: Multiple players competing for 200 crore UAV/drone orders; Solar is one of the interested participants
items.quote: This can be a big opportunity for the defense market. And as far as this program is concerned, plenty of companies will be participating. And we are also one of those companies who are interested to participate in this program.

items.statement: Forex loss 0.8-1% above normal bandwidth in Q1 due to multi-currency operations
items.quote: So around 0.8% to 1% we lost additional loss because of that.

items.statement: Staff cost increased 0.7% due to hiring for new product expansion and capital base growth
items.quote: If you look at the staff cost also, there was increase of around 0.7% in the [inaudible 0:37:56]

items.statement: GST rate on ice cream reduced from 18% to 5%; paneer tax removed but input tax credit not available
items.quote: Ice cream where it was 18% tax now it is brought down to 5%. Paneer we are there Paneer is getting removed but Paneer what has happened the input tax credit will not be available.

items.statement: Company plans to pass roughly half the GST benefit to farmers and half to consumers
items.quote: In fact, we are already working on passing almost half the benefit to the farmer and half the benefit to the consumers on whatever we are getting it as a tax exemption.

items.statement: Chairman expects GST reform to stimulate demand and increase rural spending capacity substantially
items.quote: This will stimulate demand. Not only that, the rural spending capacity will increase substantially over the period.

items.statement: Ice cream prices may come down by about 8-9%; milk and curd prices unchanged
items.quote: definitely the prices may come down by about 8 to 9% without any difficulty.

items.statement: Expects around 20% top-line growth next year driven by GST reform and new market maturation
items.quote: I expect next year we can expect a growth of 20% in my opinion.

items.statement: Heavy capex completed in new markets Maharashtra and Telangana; capacity built for future growth
items.quote: Capex is mostly done as you said and we also did the Capex in the new markets like Maharashtra and Telangana.

items.statement: New market capacity requires time to blossom; existing and new geographies expected to drive growth
items.quote: these markets requires some blossoming. So our heavy Capex also gave a slowdown because we are building a market in a new territory.

items.statement: Brand loyalty is strong; consumers unlikely to switch milk brands
items.quote: you go to your wife and ask her to change the brand of milk what she is using she may not change the brand but she may change you I said so brand matters

items.statement: Farmer price revision to be announced in next 3-4 days; benefit shared between farmer and consumer
items.quote: Farmer price admission we are going to announce it in the next 3 4 days. We are just looking at the structure and we want to give a better benefit to the farmer

items.statement: GST benefit on butter and SMP drops from over Rs 100 to Rs 30 per 25 litres of milk
items.quote: In my last interview when I said about more than 100 rupees it goes to GST once when we are selling butter and SMP this is coming down drastically to 30 rupees.

items.statement: Tax benefit shared with farmer and consumer; not retained to improve company margins
items.quote: No no no see actually this is for 25 L of milk. What I'm saying is of 70 rupees. So half of it will go to consumer. Half of it will go to the farmer.

items.statement: Dairy cooperative price increases not uniform across the country
items.quote: Dairy cooperative prices increase is not throughout the country.

items.statement: Execution guidance for FY26 is 1.2 GW (1200 MW).
items.quote: Having commenced FY '26 on a strong note, we are very confident of achieving our execution guidance for FY '26 of 1.2 gigawatt , which is 1200 megawatt.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 raised to 18%-19% from 17%-18%.
items.quote: With that we are raising our margin guidance to 18% to 19% for the full year FY '26 from 17% to 18% earlier.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at 3.1 GW with diversified clients and mix of turnkey and equipment supply contracts.
items.quote: We have very well diversified order book of 3.1 gigawatt, comprising of marquee clients across the spectrum, and a healthy mix of turnkey and equipment supply contracts.

items.statement: New 1200 MW nacelle and hub manufacturing unit operationalized near Ahmedabad; transformer manufacturing facility commenced; blade capacity expansion planned in South India.
items.quote: We have recently operationalized our new 1200 megawatt capacity nacelle and Hub manufacturing unit near Ahmedabad, Gujarat. We have also deployed the first few set of cranes at our project sites and have commenced our transformer manufacturing facility as well, all under Inox Renewable Solutions.

items.statement: Raised INR 175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approx INR 7,400 crores.
items.quote: We have recently raised INR175 crores at Inox Renewable Solutions at a valuation of approximately INR7,400 crores.

items.statement: Scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green and merger into Inox Renewable Solutions filed in NCLT; approval expected in 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Further the scheme of demerger of substation business from Inox Green and subsequent merger into Inox Renewable Solutions has received no objections from the stock exchanges and we have filed the scheme in NCLT as well. We expect the approval to happen within next two to three quarters.

items.statement: ALMM notification for wind and wind components creates level playing field for domestic manufacturers; CERC amendment allows hybridization of existing solar/wind transmission projects above 50 MW.
items.quote: The recently notified DCR for wind through ALMM is a very strong boost for local manufacturing as bringing in a level playing field between the domestic manufacturers and certain Chinese players who are importing components today.

items.statement: Industry wind installation expected at 5-6 GW in FY26, rising to 7-8 GW and potentially 8-10 GW; 90-100 GW target by 2030.
items.quote: What we see, it should be, if I see only wind, 5 to 6 gigawatt we see within this year, going upward towards 7 to 8 gigawatt, and eventually possibly 8 to 9 or may touch 10 gigawatt also.

items.statement: Inox Wind targets execution of 2 GW next year (FY27).
items.quote: From INOX Wind point of view, we have clearly said, we are executing 1.2 gigawatt this year, and possibly taking it to 2 gigawatt next year.

items.statement: Inox Green targets portfolio growth from 5 GW to ~17 GW over next two years, majority wind.
items.quote: Inox Green is where I am extremely bullish on in terms of exponential growth which should start kicking in from this financial year as we ramp up our portfolio multiple times from 5 gigawatt currently to about 17 gigawatts over the next two years.

items.statement: Net working capital days guidance maintained at ~120 days for FY26.
items.quote: Our net working capital days would be somewhere around 120 odd days, which we continue to maintain.

items.statement: Inox Wind Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 863 cr (+32% YoY), EBITDA INR 220 cr (+39% YoY), PAT INR 97 cr (+134% YoY); executed 146 MW.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, Inox Wind has reported a revenue of INR863 crores, which is an increase of 32% Y-o-Y basis. EBITDA of INR220 crores is an increase of 39% on Y-o-Y basis. PAT of INR97 crores is again an increase of 134%. Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Inox Green machine availability averaged 95.6% for entire portfolio in Q1 FY26.
items.quote: During the quarter, the machine availability for entire portfolio averaged around 95.6 %.

items.statement: Wind O&M revenue INR 8-10 lakh/MW at 45-50% margin; Solar O&M revenue ~INR 2 lakh/MWp at ~20% margin for current 1.6 GW portfolio.
items.quote: Broadly for wind, it varies from INR8 lakh to INR10 lakh per megawatt in terms of revenues and the margins are 45% to 50% for us. And for the solar part, broadly INR2 lakh per megawatt is the revenue, which we have across all the 1.6 gigawatt of portfolio with us. And broadly the margins are at around 20% for this portfolio.

items.statement: Blade manufacturing capacity expansion underway with new facility in South India to improve access to Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh sites.
items.quote: We are strategically expanding our blade manufacturing capacity and are in process of setting up another facility in south part of India. This will improve our access to the sites in the southern states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: NCRPS eliminated from balance sheet post merger of IWEL and IWL and promoter participation in rights issue; balance sheet fortified with fundraise.
items.quote: The entire NCRPS on the balance sheet now stands eliminated post the merger of IWEL and IWL and the promoters' participation in the right issue.

items.statement: Promoters fully subscribed their entitlement of ~INR 560 crores in rights issue (oversubscribed 2.13x).
items.quote: Also, the promoters, having fully subscribed their entitlement of around INR560 crores, showcases their commitment and confidence in the company.

items.statement: Management denies negative sector outlook; asserts wind is booming with government push for 15+ GW/year targets and critical role in RTC/hybrid projects.
items.quote: I am not sure where you are reading negative reports, but fundamentally I think wind is booming. The government is pushing wind more and more. I think the targets are to be north of 15 gigawatts a year.

items.statement: Added First Energy (Thermax Group) as new customer in Q1; strategy focuses on retaining existing customers and adding new ones.
items.quote: You must have seen our first quarter announcement. We brought First Energy, of Thermax Group in our fold. So, endeavour remains -- remain with existing commerce and keep on expanding our portfolio, bringing new customers.

items.statement: Inox Green made investments in entity with ~2 GW O&M assets; actively pursuing inorganic opportunities and participating in multi-GW IPP tenders.
items.quote: We have made investments in an entity around 2 gigawatt of O &M assets and shall keep on looking for such opportunities to expand our portfolio inorganically as well.

items.statement: CERC hybridization amendment allows existing solar/wind transmission projects >50 MW to hybridize, multiplying IRSL project site infrastructure potential.
items.quote: Finally, just yesterday the C ERC notified the amendment to the connectivity and the GNA regulations for the interstate transmission system allowing hybridization of existing solar and wind transmission projects with capacity upwards of 50 megawatts. This opens up a very large opportunity for IRSL as our project site infrastructure post hybridization with sola r now increases multiple times.

items.statement: H1 execution typically 30-35% of annual guidance; ramp-up expected from Q3 onwards for FY26 1.2 GW target.
items.quote: Typically, for the wind industry, including our own company, H1 is 30% to 35% of our annual execution.

items.statement: Management declines to comment on potential future demerger of Inox Green and Inox Renewable Solutions to Inox Wind shareholders; states both are integral parts of Inox Wind.
items.quote: No, I don't think we can answer that question at this point in time but clearly both of them are integral parts of Inox Wind. And for valid reasons, I see no reason why we would be de-merging them out of Inox Wind.

items.statement: Full-year execution guidance of 1,200 MW for FY26 and 2,000 MW for FY27
items.quote: firstly we are firm on our annual guidance of 1 ,200 for this year and 2 ,000 for next year.

items.statement: Q1 execution at 146 MW; first-half split guided at 30-35% of annual target with ramp-up from Q3
items.quote: 35% is broadly the first of execution guidance out of the 1,200 megawatt, which we have guided for the full year. And we feel we are on track for it.

items.statement: Firm order book of 3.1-3.2 GW with advances and signed agreements; sold out for next two years
items.quote: we have a 3.1 gigawatt of order backlogs to be executed. At this point in time, capacity to execute on our shop floor stands at 2.5.

items.statement: Multi-gigawatt MoUs and LoIs with large corporates not announced as they are non-binding
items.quote: if you want to talk about Mo Us and LoIs, we have multi -gigawatt MoUs and LoIs sitting in our Inox Wind Limited and ecosystem across some of the largest players in India which we've not announced and spoken of because that is meaningless

items.statement: Shop floor capacity at 2.5 GW; new nacelle plant in Ahmedabad and transformer factory in Jaipur commissioned; new blade plant planned in South India
items.quote: our new nacelles plant in Ahmedabad has been commissioned now. We have a Trafo factory in Jaipur, again commissioned. We are now planning to open up a new factory in the south part of India.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity in excess of 400 MW per quarter; building more blade capacity in South India and new cell plant announced
items.quote: We already have manufacturing capacity, which is in excess of 400 megawatts. We are building more blade capacity in South of India. We've set up a new cell plant which we've announced in our quarterly results.

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margins achieved much higher than guided 16-17%; profitability driven focus with consistent upgrades
items.quote: in terms of EBITDA margins also, what we had started Inox Wind Limited and with was around 15%-odd then gradually moved on to 16%-17% for the full year of FY '25. And we achieved much higher than that for the full year

items.quote: The balance 10%, which is held by Sander, who continues as the CEO of the company going forward will be acquired in 2030, basis the actual EBITDA that the company generates in the year 2029.

items.statement: Long-term revenue growth target of 25-30% per annum sustained over many years
items.quote: We will try to grow by 25% to 30%. So, that is our target as a long-term perspective.

items.statement: Sustainable PAT margin target of 20% (+/- 1-1.5%) on standalone basis; EBITDA margin to remain flat with +/-1% variation
items.quote: But 20% plus, minus 1%-1.5% is our target for every time as far as stand-alone profit of the company is concerned.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book at Rs 2,500 crore; won Rs 200 crore new orders in FY26 so far; tender pipeline of Rs 4,000 crore
items.quote: The current order book, unexecuted orders is around Rs. 2500 crores. And we have successfully achieved two orders of worth Rs. 200 crores in this financial year also. And our pipeline, tenders in pipeline is about Rs. 4000 crores rupees.

items.statement: Expects to add Rs 600 crore orders by December, taking unexecuted order book to ~Rs 3,000 crore; can execute 40% of order book annually
items.quote: So, we can still get Rs. 600 crores rupees up to December this year. And this is a continuous process, we keep on bidding and keep on getting orders. So, Rs. 600 crores we can still get. So, it will be around Rs. 3000 crores by the end of December, the unexecuted order book.

items.statement: Sees Rs 15 lakh crore potential in urban water/wastewater; only Rs 3 lakh crore done under AMRUT so far; reuse of wastewater emerging as major driver
items.quote: So, let me tell you that about Rs. 15 lakh crores potential of the work is there only in urban cities like Municipal Corporation, municipalities and town area committees. So, we have only done 3 lakh crores in AMRUT.

items.statement: Focus on central government funded schemes (AMRUT, Namami Gange, JICA, ADB) with assured funding; not executing Jal Jeevan Mission works
items.quote: We are concerned only with the Central Government Funded Schemes like AMRUT, Namami Gange, that is NMCG and JICA and ADB funded schemes, which are given only on the basis that there are funds available for that.

items.statement: 75% revenue from water/wastewater; 20-25% from electrical transmission and building works for eligibility and electromechanical synergy
items.quote: Right now we do 75% of business in water and wastewater. And apart from that we do 20%, 25% business in electrical transmission in building works.

items.statement: No further capex planned for acquired paper manufacturing subsidiary (Brij Bihari); EMS will not pump money into it
items.quote: No, we do not plan to invest any money in this company. If the company is able to generate money to start those machineries, then it may start. But EMS Limited is not going to pump in any money in that company.

items.statement: EMS Limited is debt-free (except HAM project SPV); no plans to take debt; growth funded by internal accruals
items.quote: No, we will have to take more debt, I think this is mistaken already because we are debt-free as of now. So, we do not have any debt.

items.statement: Rain impact reduces revenue and payments proportionally; payment cycle unchanged; no working capital stress
items.quote: No, no. We are even doing the less work. So, we are getting less payments. Our payment cycle is same still whether it is a rainy season or not. So, there is no payment crisis.

items.statement: Execution skewed 35% H1 / 65% H2 due to early monsoon; normally 40%/60%; underground works affected, overground and plant works continuing
items.quote: But this year, it could remain 35% in first half one and 65% in H2 due to the rainy season. But it is not affecting our overall revenue or overall profits.

items.statement: L&T not competing in sewerage network/water supply laying tenders; only in standalone STP/WTP campus projects
items.quote: But now, mainly, the sewerage network and laying of sewers in the city area or laying of water supply line in the city area, in that, currently, in our competition, L&T has not shown anywhere.

items.statement: Holding Polymer Tech Electronics as long-term pre-IPO investment; no plan to liquidate unless market conditions improve
items.quote: Sir, it was done as a long-term investment. That investment was made before our IPO. So, now, sir, there is no thought of liquidating it.

items.statement: Order book conversion rate: 40% of unexecuted order book executable per year (based on 2.5-year avg completion period)
items.quote: So, it is very safe to assume in our industry, in our type of industry that whatever is the order book, you can execute 40% of that order book in coming year.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue may decline YoY due to monsoon; full-year FY26 guidance of 25% growth maintained
items.quote: Yes, I think that is right. But we are going to maintain our guidance for year-on-year basis.

items.statement: May scrap unused machinery at Brij Bihari if scrap value is acceptable; assessing scrap rates
items.quote: Yes, we are also thinking on that line. We are assessing the scrap value. If it is acceptable and the rates seem appropriate, then the company may decide to scrap those machineries.

items.statement: AMRUT scheme has assured funding flow (tenders only after central fund consent); no fund crisis unlike Jal Jeevan Mission
items.quote: Because all tenders are done as a mission by the state mission director and that is sent to the central government for the consent of the funds. After the consent of the fund, tender is done and tender is accepted. So, there is no issue of funds in AMRUT.

items.statement: No plan to disclose online-to-offline attribution metric quarterly

items.quote: The promoter shareholding in the merged entity on a fully diluted basis, after conversion of all the warrants and ESOP, will drop down to 47.3%.

items.quote: Both the companies remain well capitalized and cash flow generated business and sufficient assets, and are fully equipped to pursue the next growth for next 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: One is to move from market leadership to market share. We want to build, double our market share in Security and FM in India. And second is to shift from services towards solutions.

items.quote: we are finalizing a recovery plan comprising commencing arbitration and appointing a collection fund. Recoveries, if any, will be recognized in the P&L when received.

items.quote: We expect the student numbers to rise from 1.7 lakhs in FY '25 to about 2 lakhs in FY '26.

items.statement: Commerce Test Prep revenue growth projected at 22-25% for FY26 driven by exam pattern changes and new course offerings
items.quote: We have moved into now giving the synergy benefits, we have entered into company secretaries and the other foreign courses as one of the strategy, which is driving this number of 22% to 25%.

items.statement: Commerce vertical EBITDA expected to cross INR140 crores in FY26
items.quote: In terms of profitability, which is expected to cross INR140 crores in the commerce vertical alone this year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA target of INR175-180 crores for FY26 (Ind AS EBITDA INR180 crores)
items.quote: It is after rent. Ind AS EBITDA will be INR180 crores.

items.statement: Commerce vertical expected to grow at 35%+ CAGR for next 5-7 years driven by domestic and GCC demand
items.quote: We expect actually our growth to move faster going forward. So we would expect to see ourselves, as I mentioned, to keep up with industry growth, if not more, at about 35% or more CAGR.

items.statement: Veranda to retain INR125-130 crores term debt at 17.25% after QIP repayment; JKSC to be debt-free
items.quote: As part of the QIP raise, the principal debt amount came down from about INR435 crores, INR440 crores. We paid INR310 crores of principal. So the principal amount outstanding has come down to about INR125 crores, INR130 crores.

items.statement: Three new Tapasya colleges added this year; 15+ locations identified for next academic cycle under Tapasya and J.K. Shah College of Commerce brands
items.quote: This year, about three colleges are being added, predominantly in the South under the brand of Tapasya. The next set of locations for expansion through Tapasya and also through the brand of J.K. Shah College of Commerce have already been identified. We have already identified over 15 locations.

items.statement: Commerce vertical has close to 200 physical points of presence across J.K. Shah (100+ centers), Navkar, Logic, and Tapasya brands
items.quote: We have close to 200 physical points of presence in the commerce vertical. This is across, as Aditya mentioned, over 100 locations of J.K. Shah Classes. Navkar has sets of locations. Logic has multiple locations in Kerala. And under Tapasya, we have brands in Andhra, Telangana and Karnataka.

items.statement: AI adoption for multi-language content delivery, assessment automation, customer support, and telesales automation across platforms
items.quote: We are also trying it out, testing it out for various levels of assessment and customer support. And lastly, it is being experimented in some parts of Veranda for automating the telesales part of the program.

items.statement: Fees collected upfront with minimal working capital needs; annual rent INR35-40 crores
items.quote: Given the nature of the business where most of the fees gets collected upfront, it is also, in a way, not so much of a working capital-intensive business at the same time.

items.statement: Government test prep: market leader in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, expanding to Karnataka then North India
items.quote: As far as government test prep is concerned, we are very strong in the South. In Tamil Nadu and Kerala, we are sort of market leaders. We are also establishing our presence in Karnataka. And over a period after we consolidate our strength in the South, we'll look for opportunities in the North.

items.statement: Professor J.K. Shah to hold 8-10% in JKSC via existing 2% stake plus 7% ESOP allocation
items.quote: So all put together, I would think he'll be able to head up to between 8% to 10% of the company.

items.statement: Demerger requires stock exchange approvals, NCLT approval, shareholder and creditor meetings, regulatory filings
items.quote: There are multiple layers of execution, including approvals from stock exchanges, NCLT approval, shareholders and creditor meetings and related regulatory filings.

items.statement: J.K. Shah Classes close to #1 in Tamil Nadu vs KS Academy; national brand strategy vs local faculty-dependent players
items.quote: in Tamil Nadu, today, J.K. Shah Classes is a very close #2 to KS Academy. So we are there. And I think based on some of the i nternal numbers, predictions that we have, I think we have a shot at going number one in Tamil Nadu

items.statement: K-12 schools to continue using J.K. Shah Classes for CA Foundation programs post-demerger, creating cross-vertical synergy
items.quote: All our K-12 schools will continue to look at J.K. Shah classes as a preferred choice for offering CA foundation programs in all our schools.

items.statement: Demerger timeline could extend beyond 7-8 months due to regulatory approvals
items.quote: We expect this to take, and we will obviously, as a management, try to push to see if we can get this done in about 7 to 8 months, but it could potentially take a bit longer based on regulatory approvals that we get.

items.statement: QIP of INR350 crores completed; INR310 crores used to repay Ascertis debt held in Veranda XL subsidiary
items.quote: As part of QIP fundraise, so we did INR 350 crores of QIP, right, out of which we closed the majority of the Ascertis debt, which I was mentioning, INR310 crores.

items.statement: Veranda XL loan-to-equity conversion completed to simplify merger structure as 100% subsidiary
items.quote: As part of merger being contemplated, we wanted this to convert this loan to equity. So VLS now VXL being 100% subsidiary of the listed company, this loan to equity conversion will not -- will be 100% subsidiary.
